items.title: How Harley-Davidson, an American Icon, Became a Tariff Punching Bag
items.summary: Harley-Davidson has repeatedly become a target for retaliatory tariffs from foreign governments, such as the European Union and Canada, whenever the U.S. imposes new tariffs. This trend continued recently when Canada levied a 50% import duty on Harley-Davidson products in response to heightened U.S. tariffs. The company's high-profile American status makes it a convenient symbol for tariff payback.

items.title: Chip Boom to Boost Korean Companies’ Cash, Goldman Sachs Says
items.summary: Goldman Sachs analysts predict that the chip industry boom will significantly increase corporate cash for South Korean companies, with repatriated overseas earnings influencing domestic financial markets. South Korean semiconductor companies are projected to generate substantial net cash, potentially reaching 9.3% of GDP by 2027. This influx is also expected to lead to record-high wage and dividend payments from major chip companies.

items.title: Why the bull market has kept defying the bears
items.summary: Despite concerns like rising oil prices, increasing bond yields, and tighter monetary policies, the stock market, represented by the S&P 500 Index, has remained near record highs. This resilience is attributed to strong nominal growth, robust corporate earnings, contained credit spreads, and healthy consumer and corporate balance sheets. The article argues that the economy is less energy-intensive and has largely absorbed interest rate hikes, suggesting that market fundamentals are stronger than current worries.

items.title: Dollar General CEO says consumers making $100,000 a year don’t feel like high-income shoppers anymore as high gas prices and inflation reshape habits
items.summary: Dollar General CEO Todd Vasos states that even consumers earning $100,000 annually no longer feel like high-income shoppers due to persistent inflation and high gas prices. This economic pressure is causing middle-to-upper-middle-income individuals to adopt shopping behaviors typically seen in lower-income shoppers, such as frequent visits to discount stores for smaller purchases. Despite these challenges, consumers remain resilient due to continued employment, with Dollar General positioning itself to serve all demographics with its low-priced offerings.

items.title: 3 Retail Stocks Getting Crushed and the Long-Dated Options Trade on Each One
items.summary: Retail stocks like TJX Companies, Burlington Stores, and Dick's Sporting Goods are experiencing significant selloffs despite strong earnings for some, driven by rising oil prices and tightening discretionary income. Andrew Keene, an options trader, is utilizing long-dated call options (January 2028 and June 2027) on these oversold stocks, specifically TJX, BURL, and DKS, to capitalize on potential rebounds while minimizing daily time decay. His strategy involves carefully sized positions based on average true range (ATR) and relative strength index (RSI), with plans to add to positions if stocks continue to decline, emphasizing risk management over prediction.

items.title: Piper Sandler cuts Colgate-Palmolive stock price target on cost pressures
items.summary: Piper Sandler has reduced its price target for Colgate-Palmolive to $95 from $98, citing elevated oil prices as a source of incremental cost pressure expected in the first half of 2027. Despite the cut, the firm maintains an Overweight rating, noting the stock trades below the new target and is undervalued based on InvestingPro data. The company faces U.S. market pressures but benefits from strong momentum in emerging markets.

items.title: John Deere Recalls Workers for Production Boost
items.summary: John Deere is recalling over 375 employees to its Quad Cities manufacturing facilities to boost production and strengthen dealer inventory. This move, which includes workers returning to Seeding and Cylinder Operations and Harvester Works, aims to ensure equipment availability for farmers and contractors. Since January, the company has hired or recalled more than 800 employees across Iowa and Illinois to support long-term business plans and prepare for future agricultural seasons.

items.title: Should You Bet on IDCC After Dividend Hike Amid Macro Uncertainty?
items.summary: InterDigital, Inc. (IDCC) recently raised its quarterly dividend, signaling confidence in its cash-generating abilities despite market volatility. The company boasts strong licensing momentum, record recurring revenues, and an upbeat 2026 outlook, bolstered by a significant agreement with Amazon. These factors, combined with a Zacks Rank #1, suggest potential for healthy long-term growth.
